Find the area $A$ of the region in the $xy$-plane that is bounded by the curve $y=3{cos}^{2}⁡x+{sin}^{2}⁡x,$ the $x$-axis and the lines $x=-\pi $ and $x=\frac{\pi }{2},$ as shown above. Do not round the answer

$A=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The area of the region is given by

$$
A={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi /2}(3{cos}^{2}⁡x+{sin}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Recall  ${cos}^{2}⁡x+{sin}^{2}⁡x=1,$ so we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}3{cos}^{2}⁡x+{sin}^{2}⁡x & =2{cos}^{2}⁡x+({sin}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x) \\  & =2{cos}^{2}⁡x+1.\end{aligned}
$$

Here, we use the double-angle formula for cosine that involves the ${cos}^{2}⁡x$ term, given by

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2x=2{cos}^{2}⁡x-1.
$$

 

Rearranging, we have

$$
2{cos}^{2}⁡x=\operatorname{cos}⁡2x+1.
$$

Hence, the area of the region is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi /2}(2{cos}^{2}⁡x+1)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi /2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2x+1+1)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi /2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2x+2)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2x+2x)\,|}_{-\pi }^{\pi /2} \\  & =(\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{2})+2\cdot \frac{\pi }{2})-(\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot (-\pi ))+2(-\pi )) \\  & =(0+\pi )-(0-2\pi ) \\  & =\pi +2\pi  \\  & =3\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
